question.text: Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
question.clue: The Simav and Nilufer Rivers flow into its Sea of Marmara.

swap.text: After establishing the government of Ankara, this man led the War of Turkish Independence and became the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
swap.clue: This man commanded the Nineteenth Division at the Battle of Gallipoli and founded his country's Grand National Assembly at Ankara.

question.text: This sultan was surprised by Wallachian troops during the Night Attack at Targoviste [ter-GOH-vish-te], after which Vlad impaled 20,000 Turks. This sultan also invaded Serbia and captured Constantinople.
question.answerHtml: Mehmed II [accept Mehmed the Conqueror; accept “Mehmet” in place of “Mehmed”]
question.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

swap.text: Ottoman authorities exterminated these people during World War One, often by marching them into the Syrian desert. These Christian people were considered of suspect loyalty by the Ottomans.
swap.clue: Sophene and Commagene were ruled by their Orontid dynasty.

question.leadin: Many of those who orchestrated this event were assassinated during Operation Nemesis.
question.text: Identify this event in which over a million people of a certain Caucasian nationality were forcibly resettled and killed, perpetrated by the Ottoman Empire during World War I.
question.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide (accept equivalents like Armenian Massacre; prompt on “Great Crime” or “Medz Yeghern”)
question.clue: Discussion of it is suppressed today by Article 301, which has led to the persecution of Hrant Dink and Orhan Pamuk.

swap.text: After the dissolution of the Black Army, this Ottoman sultan and husband of Hurrem Sultan, also known as Roxelana, conquered Hungary in the Battle of Mohacs.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman I (accept Suleiman the Magnificent, accept Suleiman the Lawgiver; prompt on Suleiman)
swap.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

question.text: The Janissaries were disbanded before this period of 19th-century reforms, which began with the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. Its modernizing provisions included ending a tax on non-Muslims and nationalizing the census.
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.text: You probably know that the Ottomans lost at the Battle of Lepanto, but more damaging was the increasing cost of employing these mostly-Christian infantrymen, recruited through the devshirme system.
swap.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

question.text: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.
question.answerHtml: Pasha [accept Three Pashas or İsmail Enver Pasha or Mehmed Talaat Pasha or Ahmed Cemal Pasha or Djemal Pasha]
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about developments in printing outside of Europe.
swap.text: Two edicts banning printing in the Ottoman empire were issued by Bayezid II and an emperor with this name. That emperor with this name conquered Egypt and was known as "the grim".
swap.clue: The first man to rule with this name was victorious at the Battle of Chaldiran over the Safavid ruler Isma'il I. A sultan of this name known as "The Blond" captured Cyprus but lost at Lepanto.

question.leadin: This battle is considered to be the turning point in the Ottoman conquest of Europe.
question.text: Name this 1529 clash that marked the farthest reach of Ottoman troops into the west. At this battle, Niklas Graf Salm defended a Habsburg city from siege.

swap.leadin: John Julius Norwich's book Four Princes focuses on Charles V, Henry VIII, Francis I and this ruler.
swap.text: Name this ruler who patronized the prolific architect Sinan. The highly detailed Piri Reis world map was created during the reign of this ruler by one of his star admirals.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [accept Kanunî Sultan Süleyman; accept Suleiman the Lawgiver]
swap.clue: At the Battle of Mohacs, this ruler's forces killed Louis II, after which this ruler threw his support behind John Zapolya.

question.leadin: The Polish slave and translator Albertus Bobovius compared this institution to a monastery.
question.text: Name this institution located in the Topkapı palace whose guards were led by the Chief Black Eunuch. Holders of the title of valide, such as Roxelana, were at the top of this institution's hierarchy.
question.answerHtml: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire [or the Seraglio]
question.answer: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire
question.clue: Talking to members of this institution demystifies it per the letters of Mary Wortley Montagu, which also discussed inoculation.

swap.leadin: Prior to the landings at this battle, the HMS Ocean sunk while trying to rescue the Irresistible, which, along with the Inflexible, had struck a line of mines laid by the Nusret.
swap.text: Name this campaign in which forces under Ian Hamilton attempted to seize Seddulbahir and Ariburnu against forces whose leaders included Ataturk.
swap.clue: William Birdwood coordinated his attack on Hill 60 with another assault on Scimitar Hill during this campaign, though both offensives failed.

question.text: Soon after the Auspicious Incident, the Ottoman army was modernized during this wider initiative. The introduction of paper money and post offices, as well as units called vilayets, were among the changes introduced during this initiative.
question.clue: This period begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber.

swap.text: In 1923, Ataturk's government negotiated this treaty with the Allied forces occupying Turkey. This treaty overturned the Treaty of Sevres ("SEV-ruh"), which would have ceded eastern Thrace and part of the Anatolian coast to Greece.
swap.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

question.text: This 1920 pact between the victorious Allied powers abolished the Ottoman Empire and provided for Armenian independence and an autonomous Kurdistan.
question.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

swap.text: This Ottoman sultan was assasinated at Kosovo by Milosh Obilic, leading to temporary confusion in the Ottoman ranks before this man's son Bayezid went on to kick some Serbian ass.
swap.clue: A Serbo-Magyar coalition that invaded his territory was crushed at the Battle of the Maritsa River.

question.leadin: The first post-Communist president of Croatia has a name indicating that one of his ancestors was one of these figures.
question.text: Give this term for people who served as liaisons between Middle Eastern and European polities. Many of these people were killed in the Phanar quarter of Constantinople after the outbreak of a certain conflict.
question.answerHtml: dragomans [prompt on interpreters or similar answers] (The Croatian president is Franjo Tudjman.)
question.clue: Because of Turkish aversion to learning non-Muslim languages, many of these imperial translators were Greeks from the Orthodox millet. These translators became de facto diplomats by virtue of their familiarity with the West.

swap.text: The Ottoman forces at Nicopolis were led by this sultan, who later died while imprisoned by Tamerlane.
swap.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.
